title: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function and the four types
guide: Ciliopathies are hereditary cystic disorders of the kidney in which a ciliary defect strips the tubular epithelium of its differentiated phenotype; polycystin regulates this function. The TYPES flowchart gives four entities: ADPKD, ARPKD, juvenile nephronophthisis and MCDK.

title: ADPKD: genes, Ravinson's criteria, renal and systemic features
guide: ADPKD is autosomal dominant with variable expression, 10% spontaneous mutations, multiple bilateral cysts as the hallmark and only 5% of nephrons involved. PKD1 (Chr16p, 85%, polycystin 1), PKD2 (Chr4q, 15%, polycystin 2, milder), PKD3 (GANA B); polycystin in vascular smooth muscle explains HTN. Ravinson's USG criteria by age band; asymptomatic presentation, abdominal discomfort at 30–40, nocturia/polyuria from impaired concentrating capacity, least anaemia of CKD, and the complications with their prognosis indicators and stone types.

title: ADPKD management, cyst infection and transplant decisions
guide: Investigations (normal RFT, USG the IOC, MRI for ESRD risk, CT/CT urography for stones, FDG PET for cyst infection) and the MRI rule for a family member wanting to donate. Treatment lowers osmolality to reduce ADH (fluids 4–5 L/day, tolvaptan 15 mg at night with LFT monitoring), tight BP control (SBP 95–110/DBP 60–75 with ACEi/ARB), novel therapies, prevention measures, CCC antibiotics for cyst infection, transplant with irreversible extrarenal associations, and the four indications for pre-transplant nephrectomy. The brain has no cysts.

title: ARPKD: gene flowchart, complications and ultrasound
guide: ARPKD is autosomal recessive, diagnosable in utero with small medullary cysts. PKHD1 on chromosome 6 makes the fibrocystin-polyductin complex; its defect affects the cilia/centrosome complex in the collecting duct (medullary cyst) and biliary duct (congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli/biliary ectasia). Pulmonary hypoplasia kills 70% within a year, portal hypertension the remaining 30% at adolescence, ESRD rarely. USG: hyperechoic medulla with loss of corticomedullary differentiation.

title: Juvenile nephronophthisis vs MCDK (ADTKD)
guide: The side-by-side table: AR versus AD; children from 5–7 years to ESRD by 13 years versus adults from 20–25 years to ESRD by 40–50 years; NPHP1 (chr 2, nephrocystin) versus MCDK1 (chr 1) and MCDK2 (chr 16, uromodulin); pathology of tubular basement membrane irregularity, tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis; clinical features with rickets-like changes; extrarenal syndromes Senior Loken, Cogan, Joubert with situs inversus; and absent recurrence after transplant in both.

title: ADPKD vs ARPKD vs juvenile nephronophthisis and medullary sponge kidney
guide: The three-way comparison table across age, kidney size, cysts, cyst infection, BP, nephrocalcinosis, CNS and liver manifestations and chromosomes. Then medullary sponge kidney — not a ciliopathy, acquired, 30–50 years, F > M in India, no CKD risk — with its pathogenesis (terminal collecting duct malformation), triad, associations (incomplete distal RTA in 50%), investigations (paintbrush/bouquet on excretory urography) and treatment, ending with the medullary versus cortical nephrocalcinosis lists and the oxalosis exception.
